PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Referral Reason: Amniocentesis for prenatal chromosome analysis
Gestational Age at Sampling: [redacted] weeks
Indication: Prenatal screening for trisomy syndromes

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Rapid aneuploidy detection for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured amniocytes obtained from amniotic fluid. QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific to chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. The following markers were analyzed:

Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1414

PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak area ratios were calculated for informative markers.

RESULTS

CHROMOSOME 13 ANALYSIS
Informative markers: 3/4
D13S631: 1:1 ratio (normal)
D13S258: 1:1 ratio (normal)
D13S742: Uninformative (homozygous)
D13S628: 1:1 ratio (normal)
Conclusion: Normal diallelic pattern consistent with two copies of chromosome 13

CHROMOSOME 18 ANALYSIS
Informative markers: 4/4
D18S535: 1:1 ratio (normal)
D18S391: 1:1 ratio (normal)
D18S390: 1:1 ratio (normal)
D18S386: 1:1 ratio (normal)
Conclusion: Normal diallelic pattern consistent with two copies of chromosome 18

CHROMOSOME 21 ANALYSIS
Informative markers: 3/4
D21S1435: 1:1 ratio (normal)
D21S1411: Uninformative (homozygous)
D21S1412: 1:1 ratio (normal)
D21S1414: 1:1 ratio (normal)
Conclusion: Normal diallelic pattern consistent with two copies of chromosome 21

SUMMARY
Analysis showed normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No abnormalities detected.

INTERPRETATION
The QF-PCR results indicate a normal chromosomal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21, suggesting absence of common trisomies (Down syndrome, Edwards syndrome, and Patau syndrome). This rapid screening test has a detection rate of >99% for trisomies 13, 18, and 21 in singleton pregnancies.

LIMITATIONS
- This test does not detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Mosaicism below 20% may not be detected
- Other chromosomal abnormalities are not assessed by this method
- Maternal cell contamination <20% may not be detected

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis from cultured amniocytes to follow. This will provide comprehensive chromosomal analysis including detection of structural abnormalities and abnormalities of other chromosomes not assessed by QF-PCR.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
